text:
The Flyers arrive in Columbus carrying the loudest story in the league. On Tuesday, ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported that Matvei Michkov would likely want a new start elsewhere. The Flyers told ESPN and TSN they have no trade request and no plan to move him, and Rick Tocchet denied it. Michkov, 21, led the team with 10 goals when the report broke and had said in Calgary he wanted more ice time; the same week brought a bench exchange with Nick Seeler and an NHL Trade Rumors headline about Travis Konecny calling him out. Charlie O'Connor of PHLY Sports reports Tocchet has defended how he has used Michkov. Tonight he carries our best Flyers chances: 27% to score, 56% for a point.

The frustration has a number behind it. O'Connor found that Philadelphia has lost ten games this season while leading or tied in the third period, in 21 played. Our numbers call the Flyers better than their record: a goal difference of -21 against -15.0 expected, with finishing costing them nearly ten goals. They close a five-game road trip at 1-1-2, and Joseph Woll is confirmed in net, five goals better than expected this season.

Columbus has its own slide. The Blue Jackets are winless in three, outscored 12-4, and the chances say that's partly real (46% of the expected goals, the share of chance quality). Jet Greaves, confirmed again, is 0-5-0 over his last five starts with an .858 save rate, and Sean Monahan left Thursday's loss with an upper-body injury, per Daily Faceoff. The Flyers sit two points ahead of them, seventh and eighth in the Metropolitan, and our simulations give both long odds: 3% for Philadelphia, 9% for Columbus.

Our sleepers are both Blue Jackets. Mathieu Olivier, one goal from 50 in his career, plays third-line minutes but has piled up 3.4 expected goals in his last ten games, better than 93% of depth forwards: 21% to score. Adam Fantilli is 50% for a point, above his season pace of 42%, because his line creates chances. For information only.
headline: Michkov noise follows the Flyers into Columbus
